To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reaction between tetracyonoethylene (TCNE), an electron-deficient alkene, and strained, electron rich dibenzo-fusced cyclooctyne is a highly accelerated, strain-accelerated [2+2]-cycloaddition-retrocyclization (CARE) reaction.
the rates of CA-RE between electron-rich alkynes and electron-poor TCNE are up to 5000 times faster when using strained, eight-membered ring substrates.
strained, cyclic alkynic compounds react up to 55000 times faster than unstrained alkynes with tetracyanoethene to form chiral, optinally active buta- 1,3-dienyl compounds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of chiral, configurationally stable buta-1-3-diene derivatives that are accessible by a strain-accelerated CA-RE reaction.
the use of ring strain to control the rate of a reaction, and with the use of the resulting products in a new synthetic method.
the synthesis of optically pure butadiene derivatives, the kinetics of the CA-RE reaction, and the enantiomerizations of these compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
strained cyclic alkynes undergo cycloadditions to electron-deficient alkynes with high rates, leading to the formation of chiral buta -1,3-dienyl products.
the CA-RE reaction is a viable method for the synthesis of chiral, configurationally stable buta-1.3-dienes.
strained, electron-rich alkynes react with TCNE to form cyclobutenes and that these cyclobutenes undergo retroelectrocyclization to form buta-1,3-dienes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ring strain of the cyclooctyne reactants is the key factor for the success of this reaction.
the use of strained cyclic alkynes in the CA-RE reactions can be used to accelerate the formation of optically pure buta-1-3-dienes.

the CA-RE reaction of TCNE with dibenzocyclooctyne derivatives is a powerful tool for the preparation of chiral, configurationally stable, optically active, and highly strained, electron-rich buta-1-3-diene compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ring strain in the cyclic alkynes accelerates the cycloaddition reaction, and that this acceleration is sufficient to allow the isolation of chiral products that can be separated by chiral chromatography.
strained, cyclic alkyl- and aryl-substituted alkynes are excellent substrates for CA-RE reactions with TCNE.
the use of strained alkynes as reaction partners can accelerate the CA-RE reaction by orders of magnitude.
